analysis.title: 3Q Mobile Ad Tech Preview: A Mixed Bag - Latest Thoughts on APP, U, LFTO
key_insights: DB lowers AppLovin (APP) 4Q26 revenue growth to 35% y/y (prior 44%) and FY27 growth to 25% (prior 32%), reflecting a more measured ramp in Gaming and Consumer. 3Q growth outlook is little changed at +47.7% y/y.
APP price target cut to $450 from $580, Buy maintained. The target rests on 18x EBITDA and 23x EPS on FY27 estimates (prior 22x and 27x).

Checks suggest APP's recent growth is concentrating in Consumer and IAA/blended campaigns rather than another step-function gain in IAP. Gaming faces scale and penetration limits on sustaining historical growth rates.
DB has heard growing concerns that Meta is scaling its audience network business more aggressively, with limited impact on APP so far.

APP Consumer remains the larger upside. APP has less than 1% merchant penetration, but AXON may need many more advertisers and much more transaction data to perform across verticals, so DB now models a slower flywheel build through 2027.

The AXON algo improvement delayed from 2Q went live in July. Checks suggest IAP performance improved from 1Q/2Q levels without a material increase in spend yet. A larger architectural change with more GPU inference could follow, with benefits showing more in incremental revenue dollars than percentage lifts.

Mixed APP expert checks: one gaming expert saw APP wallet share fall q/q, mostly from one title. A Consumer expert saw 3Q spend growth slow about 500bps from 2Q but still called performance exceptional and expects Consumer spend to exceed Gaming in 4Q.
DB cuts APP FY27 Adj. EBITDA to about $8.3-8.5bn, from a prior figure about 6.2% higher, and trims medium-term margin assumptions because larger models may need more training and inference spend.

Unity (U): DB raises 3Q26 revenue estimate to $570mn from $560mn (+21% y/y, prior +20%), FY27 revenue to $2,835mn from $2,800mn, and FY27 Adj. EBITDA to $1,095mn from $1,081mn. Buy and $50 target maintained (21x FY27E EBITDA, 29x EPS).

Unity's Vector grew 23% q/q in 2Q, driven by better model performance and higher advertiser spend. Runtime (over 90% of eligible developers opted in), 28 Day ROAS objectives, Commerce and Spark are further upside drivers. One gaming expert still struggles to scale Vector beyond one UA game.
Liftoff (LFTO): estimates unchanged, Buy kept, price target cut to $27 from $37 on 10x FY27E Adj. EBITDA (prior 13x), reflecting a discount to ad-tech peers and lower market multiples.
Liftoff shares have trended lower since 2Q26 results on macro concerns, a likely conservative 3Q guide, IPO lock-up overhang and weak investor appetite for private-equity-owned companies.

LFTO 3Q revenue guide of $217-222mn implies about -1% to +1% q/q, versus a ~4% historical baseline and ~10% q/q DAR growth in 3Q25. DB reads it as conservative, with Cortex as a durable growth engine and possible World Cup pull-forward into 2Q.
DB's channel checks say Liftoff is a key partner for Kalshi and Polymarket and should benefit from prediction market ad spend, which could continue in 4Q26 around the midterm elections.

market_movers.rationale: Target cut from $580 on lower 4Q26 and FY27 growth estimates and lower multiples. Consumer remains the long-term opportunity.
Estimates raised on Vector acceleration and high incremental margins.
Target cut from $37 on a lower EBITDA multiple. Estimates unchanged and the 3Q guide is seen as conservative.

sector_views.rationale: Gaming is healthy, but APP's scale limits growth. Consumer and Unity Vector are the growth drivers, and multiples are lower.

earnings_insights: APP 3Q26 (preview): DB models revenue growth +47.7% y/y (estimate, 30bps above prior) and Adj. EBITDA margin 83.6% (estimate, down from 84%). Historically APP has beaten the high end of its y/y revenue guide by about 5 pts, but last quarter it came in about 110bps below the guide midpoint. DB models 3Q near the high end of guidance.

APP 4Q26 (DB estimate): revenue +35.6% y/y and +8% q/q (prior +44% and +15%), Adj. EBITDA $1,894mn (prior $2,048mn), margin 84.2% (prior 86.0%). DB does not rule out double-digit q/q 4Q guidance given Consumer seasonality (4Q25 revenue grew about 65% q/q).
APP FY27 (DB estimate): revenue growth about +25% y/y (prior +32%), Adj. EBITDA about $8.3-8.5bn, about 30bps below consensus.
U 3Q26 (DB estimate): revenue $570mn (prior $560mn), +21% y/y, Adj. EBITDA $189mn (prior $187mn). Company 3Q guidance implied low- to mid-80% incremental margins.
LFTO 3Q26 (company guidance): revenue $217-222mn, about -1% to +1% q/q. DB leaves its estimates unchanged.
risk_factors: APP: increased competition, lower-than-expected Consumer take rates, regulatory headline volatility, and multiple contraction if growth slows.
Unity: deceleration could hurt multiples, delays in using Runtime data for ads, and FX/geopolitical exposure from international revenue.
Liftoff: dual-class structure with controlling shareholders, intensifying competition, mobile OS privacy policies, slower growth or lower margin conversion, and limited float with lock-up overhang.
Meta scaling its audience network business more aggressively.
vol_and_positioning: LFTO has limited float of about 22mn shares (about a ninth of the diluted share base), with potential overhang until the 180-day lock-up expires.

tension_points.bull_case: Consumer spend is strong, APP has less than 1% merchant penetration, and more advertisers and data should improve AXON performance and expand addressable spend.
tension_points.bear_case: Scaling may need a much larger advertiser base and more transaction data. Gaming growth is gated by scale, and Consumer spend growth slowed about 500bps in 3Q per one expert.
tension_points.what_invalidates: More discrete advertiser onboarding growth would lead DB to raise Consumer contribution. Slower growth could cause multiple contraction.

theme_stances.key_argument: Lower estimates require less contribution from future model improvements and Consumer onboarding, while Buy is maintained.
theme_stances.evidence: our lower estimates now simply require less contribution

theme_stances.key_argument: Model efficiencies are the primary growth driver, and Vector's high incremental margins lift EBITDA.
theme_stances.evidence: Vector's recent acceleration represents a durable improvement

theme_stances.key_argument: The flat 3Q guide embeds conservatism rather than weaker demand, and Cortex looks like a durable growth engine.
